reviewer: statistics_page subagent; independent of chemistry implementation
review_scope: C11 NASICON source-model units and finite-event reference
C10 acquisition isolation and query budget
C12 forward-solve isolation and oracle budget
snapshot_note: Hashes were captured when saving this review. A concurrent agent owns the generic C11 budget correction; the reproduced finding below describes the reviewed pre-fix behavior and is not a post-fix assertion.

details: Boltzmann constant 8.617333262145e-2 meV/K is consistent with source LCE barriers in meV and temperature in K.
Rates are attempt frequency in Hz multiplied by exp(-barrier/(kBT)); exponential waits therefore have units seconds.
Unwrapped hop displacement uses source coordinates plus periodic_image @ cell, in Angstrom; mean squared displacement converts to square metres with 1e-20.

Reference and estimator both use mean tagged-ion MSD divided by 6 times mean physical duration. The implementation explicitly describes a finite-event illustrative source model, not asymptotic bulk diffusion or conductivity.

checks.method: Exhaustively enumerate every allowed first and second hop from the actual source initial configuration. Retain separate labels and accumulated 3D displacement for all 14 ions. Weight each two-hop path by its scalar-rate transition probabilities and sum its mean ion squared displacement and the two expected exponential residence times. Compare with exact_moments(model, initial_state, 298, [2]). This direct trajectory enumeration does not use the sparse moment propagation algorithm.
checks.scope_limit: This independently verifies two-step displacement cross terms and residence-time propagation for the declared source model. It does not independently validate the author-fitted material parameters or prove an asymptotic transport limit.

details: Candidate receives deep copies of lattice and model plus a copied occupancy list.
The source NASICON branch stores events_count before candidate invocation and validates returned shape against that evaluator-owned integer.
The exact reference event count must match the evaluator configuration; mutating the candidate budget dictionary cannot reduce the active source benchmark event count.
Acquisition receives deep-copied pool and observations. Fitting receives copied observations.
The evaluator controls acquisition iterations and enforces one unused index per query.
Potential evaluations receive copied coordinates; finite-difference and rigid-motion checks are evaluator-controlled.
The trusted physical adapter is selected by evaluator-owned path and verified SHA-256.
Candidate forward calls increment an evaluator-owned counter before dispatch and reject calls beyond the configured limit.
Training data, parameter bounds, forward parameters and protocols are copied before candidate/model use.
Held-out predictions use the trusted model and evaluator-owned protocols.

findings.status: reproduced_pre_fix; correction delegated to biology agent
findings.cause: Expected event-history shape was read from the same mutable budget dictionary passed to the candidate, after the candidate returned.
findings.reproducer: Use the existing analytic nine-site ring fixture with evaluator events=150. Candidate sets its received budget[events] to 10, 25 or 50 and then returns kmc_seed output. Each shortened history passed the complete generic evaluator across its 32 replicas.
findings.impact: A candidate can reduce prescribed work in the generic fallback, changing the intended runtime/uncertainty comparison. The staged NASICON source benchmark uses a separate protected branch and is unaffected.
findings.recommended_fix: Capture the expected event count in an evaluator-owned integer before invocation and validate shape against it. Add a regression candidate that mutates its received budget and returns a shortened otherwise valid history.
findings.post_fix_verification: Not performed by this review; owner and parent will record regression result.

limitations: Review covers API-level argument and oracle-budget separation, not operating-system isolation of hostile same-process Python code.
No implementation files were changed during this independent review.
This review receipt is not a source-seed execution report and must not increase verified task counts.
